info.title: Neon Teamspace API
info.description:
The HTTP API of Neon Teamspace.

Every error response has the same body: `{"error": {"code": string, "message": string}}`. `code` is stable and meant for programs, such as `not_found` or `invalid_json`; `message` says what went wrong, for people. A body that is not JSON answers `400 invalid_json`; JSON with a field missing, unknown or of the wrong type answers `400 invalid_input`, its message naming the field. A request with several wrong fields, such as settings, also lists each in `problems`, and a refused claim lists who holds the row in `holders`. A rate-limited request answers 429 with `Retry-After`.

A request authenticates with the session cookie that `POST /api/v1/auth/login` sets, or with `Authorization: Bearer nw_…`, an API token. A token's scopes decide what it may do: `read` for safe methods, `write` for the others, `admin` for `/api/v1/admin`. A token bound to a workspace works on that workspace's routes and sockets alone, and is refused on another's, on `/api/v1/account` and on `/api/v1/admin` with `token_bound`; its `admin` scope adds that workspace's admin work. An agent's token is always bound to the agent's workspace and acts as the agent, which may do only what both it and its owner may. An OAuth access token, `nwo_…` from `POST /api/v1/oauth/token`, is sent the same way and works as a token bound to the workspace its person chose, acting as them or as one of their agents. The OAuth endpoints for clients, `/api/v1/oauth/register`, `/token` and `/revoke`, answer errors in OAuth's own shape, `{"error": code, "error_description": text}`, and allow CORS from any origin. Deleting a workspace and transferring its ownership need a browser session. A request that changes something and carries no `Authorization` header must come from the server's own origin: its `Origin`, or else its `Referer`, must match the public URL.

get.description: The authorization endpoint, the code flow with PKCE (S256 alone). Checks the client, the redirect URI, the response type, the PKCE challenge, the scopes, the state and the resource, then sends the browser to the web app's consent page with them, where the person signs in if they have not, and chooses. A request that does not hold sends the browser to the consent page with `error`, its problem, which the page shows; it is never sent to the client's redirect URI on its own, as anyone may register one.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: One the client registered, exactly, but for the port of a loopback address.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The PKCE challenge: the verifier's SHA-256, in base64url without padding.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Scopes asked for, space-separated: `read`, `write`, `admin`. The person chooses.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Sent back as it is; at most 1024 printable ASCII characters.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
The resource the tokens are for (RFC 8707): `<public URL>/mcp`, the default, or
`<public URL>/api/v1`.

302.description: To the consent page, with the request or `error`.

post.summary: What a client asks to be allowed
post.description: Checks an authorization request again, from the consent page's address, and says what the page offers: the client, where the browser goes back to, and each of the person's workspaces with whom the client may act as there, the person or one of their agents that works, and with which scopes. Only reads. From a browser session alone.

400.description: The request's problem: duplicate_parameter, missing_client_id, unknown_client, missing_redirect_uri, redirect_uri_mismatch, unsupported_response_type, pkce_required, invalid_code_challenge, invalid_scope, invalid_state or invalid_target.

post.description: Grants the client what the person chose, from a browser session alone: the workspace, whom it acts as, the person or one of their agents that works there, and scopes among those offered. Consenting again to the same client, workspace and identity replaces the grant's scopes. Answers where to send the browser: the client's redirect URI with a code that works once, within a minute, with the request's PKCE verifier.

400.description: The request's problem, as for /oauth/consent, or invalid_scope.

403.description: forbidden, or identity_unavailable: acting as that identity is off, or the agent does not work.

404.description: not_found: no such workspace or agent.

post.description: Answers where to send the browser when the person denies the client, from a browser session alone: its redirect URI with `error=access_denied`.

Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), open to anyone while `oauth.registration` is on, a few at a time from one address or IPv6 /64, and a few waiting unconnected from each. Every client is public, with no secret: it proves itself with PKCE. Allows CORS from any origin. Errors are in OAuth's shape.

413.description: invalid_client_metadata: a body larger than 64 KiB.

429.description: rate_limited, with Retry-After; or too_many_clients: too many clients registered from the same address, or IPv6 /64, wait unconnected.

503.description: temporarily_unavailable: too many clients wait unconnected.

post.description: Token revocation (RFC 7009): revokes the grant of an access or refresh token, every token of it, as a client does when it signs out. A token that is unknown, or another client's, changes nothing, and the answer is the same. Allows CORS from any origin. Errors are in OAuth's shape.

413.description: invalid_request: a form larger than 16 KiB.

post.summary: Exchange a code or a refresh token
post.description: The token endpoint. `authorization_code` exchanges a code, within its minute and once, with its redirect URI and PKCE verifier; `refresh_token` exchanges a refresh token, once. Each gives an access token, an hour by default, and a new refresh token, 30 days by default. A code or refresh token used a second time revokes its grant and every token of it. Allows CORS from any origin. Errors are in OAuth's shape.

400.description: invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_scope, invalid_target or unsupported_grant_type.

413.description: invalid_request: a form larger than 16 KiB.

What markdown cannot hold, such as colours, is left out. Each caller may export 10 times, then once more every 30 seconds.

post.summary: Upload a file to a page
post.description: Uploads a file for one of the page's image, video, audio or file blocks, or its cover, for those who edit the page, out of the trash. Its type comes from its bytes, whatever the client says, and must be one the kind takes. It streams to the file store as it comes, and counts against the workspace's storage limit, which refuses it once reached. Give the answer's `url` to the block, or its `id` to the page as `cover_image`. Each caller may upload 60 files at once, then one more a second; an upload may take 15 minutes.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The kind of block the file is for, whose types it must be of.

file.description: The file, its name as the part's filename. At most `attachments.max_file_bytes`.

400.description: invalid_input: a form whose first part is not `file`; or invalid_body, a form that cannot be read or stopped short.

403.description: forbidden: the caller views the page and does not edit it, or it is in the trash; or insufficient_scope.

409.description: storage_limit: the workspace has no room for the file.

413.description: file_too_large: past attachments.max_file_bytes, said as it arrives or as declared; or payload_too_large, a form whose file does not start within its first 64 KiB.

415.description: unsupported_type: the file's bytes are of a type the kind does not take.

503.description: storage_unavailable: the file store did not answer.

put.summary: Follow a page's comments, or stop
put.description: Who follows a page hears of every comment on it in their inbox. Its maker, and whoever comments on it or is mentioned on it, follows it until they stop.

get.description: Its blocks as markdown, each block's id on a line of its own before it, `<!-- block <id> -->`, which the edits name, and for a row its properties with their values; and the revision they are at, which an edit replacing blocks names as its base. A database has no body of its own: read its rows.

patch.description: Makes the operations in order, all or none, through the page's live document: whoever has the page open sees the change at once, and what they type meanwhile merges with it. Operations name blocks by the ids reading the markdown shows. replace_range and replace_body need base, the revision the markdown they were made from was read at: once the page is at another, they are refused, as they would remove what was added or changed since. Editing needs edit access to the page, out of the trash. A page holds at most 16 MiB. Each user has 100 edits at once, through this route and MCP together, then two a second.

400.description: invalid_input: no operations or more than 50, markdown nesting blocks more than 32 levels deep, or a database; base_required: replace_range or replace_body without base; edit_refused: an operation names a block the page lacks or blocks that are no range, or its text is not in the page, there more than once, or with all more than 10000 times, or its blocks would go in so far into a long page that one edit's writes pass more than 4000000 blocks, and nothing changed.

403.description: forbidden: the caller views the page and does not edit it, or it is in the trash; or insufficient_scope.

read.description: Marks it read, or unread again.

NotificationList.description: A part of an inbox, newest first.

next.description: Pass it back as `before` for the next part; absent at the end.

NotificationSettings.description: How the caller wants mail of their inbox, and whether the instance sends it.

digest_interval_secs.description: How often, at most, a digest goes, in seconds.

mail_available.description: The instance sends notification mail now; off, the preference waits until it does.

NotifiedInvitation.description:
An invitation a notification is, while it waits for an answer, which
`POST /account/invitations/{id}/accept` and `/decline` answer.

NumberFormat.description: How a number shows; values are any finite number whatever the format.

OAuthErrorBody.description: An error as OAuth's endpoints answer it (RFC 6749, section 5.2).

error_description.description: What went wrong, for whoever reads the client's logs.

OAuthResource.description: What the resource a client asked for is.

Operator.description:
How a condition compares a row's value with its own; which a property takes depends on
its type, as the databases reference lists.

OptionChange.description: An option as a change lists it: an existing one by its id, a new one without.

oneOf.description: For a status option, which needs one.

hue.description: 0 to 359; none draws it in grey.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters, unique in the property, ignoring case.

Owner.description: The person an agent or integration acts for.

Page.description: A page, without its content, and what the caller may do with it.

cover_image.description:
An image uploaded to the page, shown as its cover in place of `cover`, whose bytes
are at `/api/v1/files/{cover_image}`.

created_by.description: Absent for guests, as are `last_edited_by` and `trashed_by`.

last_edited_by.description: Who changed it last, its content included.

owner_id.description:
The member a private page belongs to; absent for a teamspace's page, and for
guests, who know no other member.

parent_id.description:
The page it is under; absent at the top of its space, and when the caller may not
see that page.

position.description: Its key among its siblings, which sort by it, byte by byte.

teamspace_id.description: The teamspace it is in; absent for a private page.

title.description: Up to 500 characters; empty shows as Untitled.

trashed_at.description: Set while it is in the trash.

trashed_with.description:
While it is in the trash: the page trashed with it, itself when it was trashed on
its own. Restoring that page brings this one back too.

updated_at.description: When its title, icon, cover, style or place last changed.

PageAccess.description: What the caller may do with a page.

markdown.description: Its blocks as markdown, each after a line `<!-- block <id> -->` that names it.

properties.description: For a row: each property of its database, in order, with the row's value.

revision.description:
The revision of what `markdown` shows, which changes whenever it does: an edit that
replaces a range or the body sends it as its `base`.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next part; absent on the last one.

pages.description:
Each page, then the pages under it, siblings in order: a page's parent comes before
it, in this part or an earlier one.

blocks.description: Its blocks in BlockNote's JSON, as `/ws/pages/{id}` would give the editor them.

markdown.description:
Its blocks as markdown, each after a line `<!-- block <id> -->` that names it, as
`GET /pages/{id}/markdown` writes them.

Person.description:
A person as the people they work with see them, or an agent or integration with the
person it acts for: shown as `Scout · via Ada Lovelace`.

display_name.description: A person's name, or an agent's or integration's.

email.description: A person's address; absent for an agent or integration, which has none.

hue.description: The hue they are drawn in, 0 to 359.

oneOf.description:
An agent's or integration's owner, whom it acts for; absent for a person, and once
the owner's account is gone.

Placement.description:
Where a page goes among its siblings: `"first"`, `"last"`, `{"after": id}` or
`{"before": id}`, the id being a sibling's.

PostedComment.description:
A comment just made or changed, with its thread, and those it mentions who may not see
the page: they were told nothing, and sharing the page with them would let them.

Preferences.description: The look of the web app, kept with the account.

accent_hue.description:
The user's own accent, a whole number of degrees, 0 to 359. Absent or null, the
accent is the hue of the workspace in view, or a blue outside any.

key.description: The field, such as a setting's key.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the currency format.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters, unique in the database, ignoring case.

oneOf.description: A number's format.

options.description: A select's, multi-select's or status's options, in order.

prefix.description: A unique id's prefix, before the row's number.

PropertyOption.description: An option of a select, multi-select or status property.

oneOf.description: A status option's group; absent for the others.

id.description: Values hold it by its id, so renaming it keeps them.

QueryAnswer.description: A part of a query's answer.

groups.description: For a view that groups: every group, in its order, hidden ones too.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next part; absent on the last one.

rows.description: In order; grouped, in the order of the groups, a row once in each group it is in.

total.description: How many entries the whole answer holds.

QueryGroup.description: A group of a grouped query.

count.description: How many rows that passed the filter it holds.

hidden.description: The view hides its rows, which the answer leaves out.

key.description: An option's id, a person's id, or null for the rows without a value.

oneOf.description: In place of the view's filter.

limit.description: Rows in the part, 1 to 1000; 100 when absent.

sorts.description: In place of the view's sorts.

utc_offset_minutes.description:
The caller's UTC offset in minutes, -840 to 840, which days are told at: `today`,
and the day a moment falls on. 0 when absent.

view_id.description:
The view whose filter, sorts and grouping to use; every row, in manual order, when
absent.

ReceivedInvitation.description: An invitation the signed-in user waits on.

oneOf.description: Who invited them; absent once that account is gone.

role.description: What they would join as: admin, member or guest.

display_name.description: The address's local part when absent.

invite_code.description: Needed while registration is by invite.

must_verify.description:
The account signs in only once it opened the link mailed to it, which was queued
with the account. Another can be asked for with `POST /auth/verification`.

client_id_issued_at.description: When it registered, in seconds since 1970.

base.description:
The revision of the page the version was compared with, as the comparison answered:
once the page is at another, the restore is refused with `edit_conflict`.

RevokeForm.description:
A request to revoke a token, a form (RFC 7009). A `token_type_hint` may come along;
the token is looked up whatever it says.

client_id.description: The client the token was issued to.

token.description: An access token or a refresh token.

Role.description: What an account may do on the instance.

Row.description: A row of a database, with its values.

database_id.description:
Its database; null for someone who sees the row only through its own share and not
its database, as its page then leaves out the page above it.

group.description:
In a grouped query, the group it is listed in: an option's id, a person's id, or
null for the rows without a value. Absent otherwise.

last_edited_at.description: When its title, values, place or content last changed.

number.description: Its number in the database, which no other row of it has had or will have.

position.description: Its key among the rows: their manual order.

unique_id.description: Its number after the unique id property's prefix, `NW-42`, or alone without one.

values.description:
Each property's value, by property id, for those it has one of. A title, text or
URL is a string; a number a number; a select or status an option's id; a
multi-select a list of option ids; a date `{"start": ..., "end": ...}`, each a day
`2026-11-22` or an RFC 3339 moment, the end optional; a person a list of members'
ids; a checkbox `true`; a unique id its text, `NW-42`; a created or last edited time
an RFC 3339 moment; created or last edited by a member's id. Guests, who know no
other member, get no person values, nor who made or changed a row.

RowProperty.description: A property of a row's database, with the row's value of it.

text.description:
The value as people read it: options and people by name, numbers in their format;
null without one.

oneOf.description: The value as rows give it, by id; null without one.

Scope.description: What an API token may do: `read`, `write`, or the admin pages' work, `admin`.

SearchResult.description: A page, database or row found.

rank.description:
How well it matched, higher being better, as the results are ordered: worth
comparing within one search only. 0 without a query.

snippet.description:
A few words of a row's property values and the text around the matches, in runs
that mark them, on one line: ` · ` stands between its lines, such as a page's blocks.
Empty without a query, or without text.

title.description: Its title, in runs that mark what matched; empty without a query.

SearchResults.description: A part of the results, the best first.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next part; absent on the last one.

SentInvitation.description: An invitation a workspace sent, waiting for its answer.

invited_by.description: Who invited them; absent once their account is gone.

role.description: What they join as: admin, member or guest.

SessionInfo.description: A browser session of the user.

current.description: The session this request came with.

members.description:
The most people, guests included: 0 for no limit, null to follow the instance's
default. Absent stays as it is.

storage_bytes.description: The most bytes of attachments, likewise.

Setting.description: A runtime setting as admins see it, with secrets redacted.

browser_only.description:
Changes only from a browser session, never with an API token: a secret, or a setting
that says where one goes, such as the mail server.

options.description: An enum's options, or those a set picks from.

pinned.description: Set by the environment or the config file, so it cannot change here.

value.description: A secret shows as `[redacted]` when set, and empty when not.

SettingSource.description: Where a setting's value comes from.

Share.description: A page shared with a member or guest.

inherited.description: Set on a page above the one listed, and holding here too; it changes there.

page_id.description:
The page it is set on: the one listed, or a page above it; absent when that is a
page above that the caller may not see.

shares.description: The page's own first, then those of each page above it, each page's by name.

SignedIn.description: A new session. Its token is only in the cookie.

absolute_expires_at.description: When it ends however much it is used.

expires_at.description: When the session ends unless it is used before.

SkipReason.description: Why a file of a zip was left out.

SkippedFile.description: A file of a zip left out of an import.

Sort.description: A sort by one property. Rows without a value come last either way.

property.description: The property, by id or name.

StatusGroup.description: The group of a status option.

StyleChange.description:
The parts of a page's style to set; each left out stays as it is, or takes its default
on a new page.

TargetKind.description: What an incoming webhook works on.

Task.description: A row assigned to the caller.

database_title.description: Its database's title, absent when the caller sees the row alone.

oneOf.description: Its value of its database's status property.

TaskList.description: The rows assigned to the caller.

tasks.description: The most recently changed first, at most 100.

TaskStatus.description: A status option, as a task holds it.

Teamspace.description: A teamspace the caller may see.

hue.description: The hue it is drawn in, 0 to 359: the one it pinned, or else its id's.

oneOf.description: The caller's role in it; absent when they are not in it.

TeamspaceAccess.description: Who sees a teamspace and who may join it.

hidden.description:
For owners and admins of the workspace: the private teamspaces they are not in, by
name only, to manage or delete them.

teamspaces.description:
The teamspaces the caller sees, the default one first, then by name. None for a
guest.

TeamspaceName.description: A private teamspace the caller is not in, by name only.

TeamspaceRole.description: What a person may do in a teamspace.

queued.description: Always true in a 202: the mail is in the queue.

TextRun.description: A run of text: a match of the query, or what is between.

highlight.description: It is what the query matched.

resolved.description: Resolves the thread, or reopens it.

ThreadList.description: A part of a page's threads, oldest first, and what the caller may do with them.

following.description: The caller follows the page's comments.

may_comment.description: The caller may start threads, reply, resolve and reopen them.

may_moderate.description: The caller edits the page: they delete others' comments, and whole threads.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next part; absent at the end.

open_threads.description: How many threads of the page are open, in every part.

ThreadOut.description: A thread of comments: on the page as a whole, or on a range of its text.

oneOf.description: Where it is, for an inline thread; absent for one on the whole page.

comment_count.description: How many comments it holds in all.

comments.description:
Its first comment, which starts it, and its latest replies after it, in order, at
most 10 in all; `GET /threads/{id}/comments` reads the rest.

ToGroup.description: A row moving between groups of a view.

from.description:
The group it leaves: for a person property, whose person makes room for the one of
`to`, the others staying. Null or absent for the group without a value.

to.description: The group it goes to: an option's id, a person's id, or null for no value.

TokenForm.description: A request to the token endpoint, a form.

client_id.description: The client, which public clients name to identify themselves.

redirect_uri.description: For `authorization_code`: the redirect URI the code was given to.

refresh_token.description: For `refresh_token`: the refresh token, which works once.

resource.description: The resource the tokens are for (RFC 8707): the one the authorization asked for.

scope.description: For `refresh_token`: fewer scopes than the refresh token had.

TokenRequest.description: The body of routes that take a token from a mailed link.

access_token.description: `nwo_` and 43 characters: send it as `Authorization: Bearer`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token stops working.

refresh_token.description: `nwr_` and 43 characters: works once, for a new access token and refresh token.

owner_id.description: The person of the workspace, not a guest, who owns it from now on.

user_id.description: The member who becomes an owner.

TrashList.description: A part of a workspace's trash.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next part; absent on the last one.

pages.description: Latest first. A page trashed with the pages under it stands for them.

TreePage.description: A page in a tree, as a sidebar shows it. Rows are not in trees: their database is.

child_count.description: How many pages are under it, out of the trash; a database's rows are not counted.

owner_id.description:
The member a private page belongs to; absent for a teamspace's page, and for
guests, who know no other member.

parent_id.description:
The page it is under; absent at the top of its space, or of the pages shared with
the caller.

hue_override.description: 0 to 359; null goes back to the id's hue.

enabled.description: False turns it off: it refuses what is sent until it is on again.

display_name.description: At most 100 characters; blank takes the address's local part.

hue_override.description: The hue to be drawn in, 0 to 359; null goes back to the one the id hashes to.

oneOf.description: Null removes it. Setting it takes `cover_image` off.

cover_image.description:
An image uploaded to the page, with `kind=image`, to show as its cover; null removes
it. Setting it takes `cover` off.

changes.description:
By key: the new value, as JSON of the setting's type, a list of options for a set,
or null to go back to the default.

oneOf.description: Open, closed or private; the default teamspace keeps its access.

hue_override.description: 0 to 359; null goes back to the id's hue.

disabled.description: Disabling signs the account out everywhere.

email_verified.description: True marks the address verified; it cannot be made false.

enabled.description: True turns it on and clears its failures; false turns it off.

oneOf.description: Who makes agents in it.

agents_enabled.description:
Turns the workspace's agents on or off. Off, none is made and every agent's tokens
are refused, its open connections closed.

hue_override.description: 0 to 359; null goes back to the id's hue.

slug.description: A new name leaves the slug as it is; this changes it.

disabled_at.description: Set while the account is disabled.

email_verified_at.description: Unset while the address must still be verified.

hue.description: The hue they are drawn in, 0 to 359: the one they pinned, or else their id's.

hue_override.description: The hue they pinned, if any.

UserKind.description: What an identity is: a person, or an agent or integration acting for one.

UserPage.description: A page of accounts in the order they were made.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next page; absent on the last one.

Verified.description: An address a link verified, for the sign-in form.

Version.description: A version of a page: its content each time the server saved it changed.

added.description:
How many blocks it added, changed and removed since the version before, at any
depth; the first version counts every block as added.

authors.description:
Who changed the page since the version before: people, agents and integrations, by
member id. Empty for guests, who know no other member.

created_at.description: When its latest change was made.

restored_from.description: For a version a restore made: the version restored, while it is kept.

restored_from_at.description: And when that one was made.

VersionList.description: A part of a page's history, latest first.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next part; absent on the last one.

View.description: A view of a database, its settings naming properties by id.

position.description: Its key among the database's views.

properties.description: Every property, in the view's order.

ViewProperty.description: A property as a view shows it, in the view's order.

property.description: The property, by id or name; answers name it by id.

width.description: Its column's width in pixels, 40 to 2000, once resized.

Webhook.description: An outgoing webhook, without its secret.

oneOf.description: Absent once their account is gone.

disabled_reason.example: turned off after 5 deliveries in a row failed; the last: the receiver answered 500

enabled.description: False while it is off: turned off by hand, or after deliveries kept failing.

failures.description: Deliveries given up on in a row since the last one that went through.

identity.description: The identity whose events it delivers, without their address.

include_own.description: Whether it is told of the identity's own changes too.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: Until when the secret before the last rotation signs deliveries too.

WebhookEvent.description:
What an outgoing webhook may be told of. Receivers ignore types they do not know: more
come later.

WebhookWithSecret.description: A webhook with its signing secret, shown this once.

secret.description: `whsec_` and 43 characters. The server keeps it encrypted and never shows it again.

WhoAmI.description: Whom a request acts as, and what it may do.

identity.description: A person, or an agent or integration with the person it acts for.

scopes.description: A session has every scope its role allows; a token, its own.

oneOf.description:
The workspace a token is bound to, while its identity is in it; absent for a session
and for a token across the instance.

member_count.description:
How many people are in it, guests included, agents and integrations left out.
Absent for a guest, who knows of no member but themselves.

members_can_create_teamspaces.description: Members, besides owners and admins, may create teamspaces.

storage_bytes.description:
The bytes its attachments take together, as `limits.storage_bytes` counts them.
Absent for a guest.

Workspace.description: A workspace the caller is in.

WorkspaceAgents.description: A workspace's agents as a whole: whether they work, and who makes them.

available.description:
Whether the instance has agents at all, as the setting `mcp.identities` says. Off,
none is made and their tokens are refused, whatever the workspace says.

count.description:
How many agents and integrations it has, deleted ones left out. Absent for a
guest.

enabled.description:
Whether the workspace has its agents on. Off, none is made and their tokens are
refused.

can_create.description: Whether the caller may create a workspace, as the `workspaces.creation` setting says.

WorkspaceRole.description: What a person may do in a workspace.

WorkspaceSummary.description: A workspace the caller is in, as their list shows it.

hue.description: The hue it is drawn in, 0 to 359: the one it pinned, or else its id's.

hue_override.description: The hue it pinned, if any.

icon.description: An emoji or a short text.

slug.description: For URLs: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, unique on the instance.

agents.description:
Its agents and integrations together, deleted ones left out, as its agent limit
counts them.

storage_bytes.description: The bytes its attachments take together, as its storage limit counts them.

api_token.description: An API token, nw_ and 43 characters, made under /api/v1/account/tokens, or an OAuth access token, nwo_ and 43 characters, from /api/v1/oauth/token.

session_cookie.name: neon_session
session_cookie.description: The browser session, set by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Named __Host-neon_session when the server's public URL is https.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Signing up, in and out, and the mailed links. Open to anyone.

tags.name: account
tags.description: The signed-in user's own account, their favorite pages, and the invitations into workspaces waiting for them.

tags.name: workspaces
tags.description: Workspaces, their members, invitations and invite links.

tags.name: agents
tags.description: A workspace's agents and integrations, members that act for a person there, and agents' API tokens.

tags.name: oauth
tags.description: The OAuth 2.1 authorization server MCP clients and other programs connect through: client registration, the authorization code flow with PKCE, tokens, revocation, the consent page's requests, and connected apps. Its metadata is at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, which the docs describe.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: Outgoing webhooks, which tell a URL, signed, of what happens to the rows an identity is assigned to, with their delivery logs; and incoming webhooks, which act as an integration on a database or page with what is posted to their URL, `POST /hooks/in/{token}`, which the docs describe.

tags.name: teamspaces
tags.description: A workspace's teamspaces and their members.

tags.name: pages
tags.description: Pages and their trees, sharing, and the trash.

tags.name: files
tags.description: Attachments: files uploaded to a page for its image, video, audio and file blocks and its cover, and read back at the path documents refer to them by, `/api/v1/files/{id}`.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Searching a workspace's pages, databases and rows by their titles, text, rows' values and comments, among those the caller may see.

tags.name: history
tags.description: Pages' versions: listing them, reading one, comparing one with the page as it is, and restoring one through the page's live document.

tags.name: comments
tags.description: Threads of comments on pages, on a page as a whole or on a range of its text, their replies, following a page's comments, and what a mention may name. Open pages' editors hear that a thread changed over `GET /ws/pages/{id}`, which the docs describe.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: The inbox: mentions, replies, comments on followed pages, assignments and invitations, each checked again against what its person may see; how one wants mail of it, and the link that stops that mail. The app follows it live at `GET /ws/inbox`, which the docs describe.

tags.name: databases
tags.description: Databases: their properties and views, and their rows with their values. A database and its rows are pages too. Their changes are followed live at `GET /ws/databases/{id}`, which the docs describe.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Accounts, invites, requests to join, settings and workspaces' limits, for instance admins.
